orders.text:
WPSS No. 607 of 2018 
Hon’ble Lok Pal Singh, J.
Mr. S.S. Yadav, Advocate for the 
petitioner. 
 Mr. K.N. Joshi, Dy. A.G. for the State. 
 No representation for respondent no. 6. 
 By means of the writ petition, petitioner 
has prayed for the following reliefs: 
 (i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the 
nature of mandamus directing the respondent nos. 
1,2,3 & 6 to provide the service benefits to the 
petitioner considering his status at this juncture. 
 (ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the 
nature of mandamus, directing the respondent 
nos. 1, 6 & 7 to produce the documents of final 
allocation for examination of the status of the 
petitioner service and its employer.” 
 Perusal of the record would reveal that 
petitioner has not filed any document in order to 
substantiate his claim that he is appointed in 
the Department. 
 In theses circumstances, petitioner is 
permitted to file supplementary affidavit in this 
regard within 15 days. 
 List thereafter. 
 No good ground is made out to grant any 
interim relief to the petitioner at this stage. 
Interim relief application is dismissed. 
 
 
(Lok Pal Singh, J.) 
 13.11.2019 Mamta

Mr. Furkan Ahmed, Advocate, for the

Mr. Gopal K. Verma, Standing 
Counsel, for the State of U.P.
In order to better elucidate the 
controversy involved in the writ petition,
because of the fact that petitioner having been 
appointed in the State is a fact which has been 
denied by the State’s Standing Counsel. So far 
as the status of initial appointment of the 
petitioner is concerned i.e. w.e.f. 01.01.1983, 
there is no material on record to show that the 
petitioner was initially and actually appointed 
on 01.01.1983, to which the learned counsel for 
the petitioner prays for that he may be granted 
three weeks’ time to place the letter of 
appointment of the petitioner on record, after 
procuring the same under the Right to 
Information Act and during this period the State 
of U.P. too would file the counter affidavit, 
bringing complete facts on record.
List this matter after three weeks.
As far as IA/15071/2021, filed by the 
respondents in reply to the rejoinder affidavit of 
the petitioner, the same is allowed. 
Supplementary counter affidavit is taken on 
record.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)

Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. S.S. Yadav, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. G.S. Negi, learned Addl. C.S.C. for 
the State of Uttarakhand.
3. Mr. I.D. Paliwal, learned Standing 
Counsel for the State of U.P.
4. Mr. Rajesh Pandey, learned C.G.C. for 
respondent no. 7/ Union of India.
5. This Court vide order dated 01.05.2024 
directed the learned Standing Counsel for 
the State of U.P. to file counter affidavit.
6. Learned counsel for the State of U.P. 
fairly submits that despite writing a letter to 
the respondent i.e. D.M. Rampur, no one is 
responding and for that reason the counter 
affidavit could not be filed. 
7. The petitioner’s case as reflected from 
the writ petition is that he was posted in a 
regular establishment as Chainman (Class￾IV post in the Survey Department) and was 
posted at Kichha in the year 1994; petitioner 
was transferred from Garh-Mukteshwar to 
Kichha in the year 1994-95.
8. In the reliving order of 78 employees
who were transferred from Garh￾Mukteshwar to Kichha, the name of the 
petitioner Furkan Ahmed was not found. 
But the respondents no. 1 to 3 have not annexed the entire list of 78 employees who 
had been transferred from Garh￾Mukteshwar to Kichha. Instead of 
mentioning the names of employees who had 
joined at Kichha, name of 25 employees who 
have not joined, are mentioned. This 
information does not clarify the things. 
Accordingly, the State of Uttarakhand shall 
file the list of those persons who had joined 
pursuant to their transfer from Garh￾Mukteshwar to Kichha.
9. Apart from that, learned counsel for 
the State of U.P. as well as the State of 
Uttarakhand are directed to bring on record 
the list of those 78 employees who had been 
transferred in the year 1994-95.
10. It is expected that officers at the 
highest level of both the States will 
coordinate and submit this information 
before this Court within three weeks.
11. List on 30.10.2026.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 30.09.2026
Nahid
